note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer management decision following stable biopsy findings and rising PSA.

The patient is a 70-year-old mechanical engineer, never married, living with his partner. He has a history of hypercholesterolaemia, COPD, and osteoarthritis. Medications include atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, tiotropium, and salbutamol PRN. He is a non-smoker, alcohol-free, and plays tennis twice weekly. IPSS score is 28/35, indicating severe LUTS. He has visual impairment requiring large-print correspondence. Recent appointments include a memory clinic baseline screening and biannual dental check-up. PSA trend: 2.9 ng/mL (Dec 2022), 3.7 ng/mL (Jan 2024), 4.8 ng/mL (Jan 2025).
Per rectum, the prostate feels smooth and symmetrically enlarged without nodules, consistent with cT1c. General examination is unremarkable. Visual impairment noted; large-print materials provided.
